page_title: Native Screen: Record once. It comes out edited.

sources.entry: Native Screen - Open-source screen recorder and editor with a multi-track timeline, auto-zoom, and on-device captions. [![Open-Source Software][OSS Icon]](https://github.com/maitrungduc1410/NativeScreen) ![Freeware][Freeware Icon]

summary.name: Native Screen
summary.one_liner: Native Screen is a free, open source screen recorder and editor for macOS and Windows that turns raw recordings into polished demos with auto-zooms, captions and a multi-track timeline.
use_cases: Make tutorial videos with zooms and captions
Create vertical videos for TikTok, Reels or Shorts
Edit screen recordings offline without uploads
Let an AI agent edit a screen recording
summary.what_it_does: Native Screen records the screen and automatically creates zooms from clicks and typing, which can be moved, changed in depth, or switched to a loupe. Its editor has a multi-track timeline with separate lanes for zooms, blurs, captions, keycaps, text, arrows, shapes and images, with snapping, trimming, splitting and undo. It smooths shaky cursor paths, adds motion blur to fast moves, and shows pressed keyboard shortcuts as keycaps. Users can draw annotations live during recording, switch between wide, square and vertical layouts, and blur or replace backgrounds. It also exposes an MCP interface so agents such as Claude or Cursor can record, edit and export within the open editor.
notable: Open source under MIT license, with source on GitHub
Runs locally with no account, upload or telemetry
Native builds using SwiftUI/AppKit/Metal on Mac and WinUI 3/Direct3D 11 on Windows, without FFmpeg or a browser engine
Projects stored as documented JSON folders that open on both Mac and Windows
caveats: Windows installer from GitHub is not code-signed, so SmartScreen warns on first run; the Microsoft Store version is signed
Requires macOS 14 or later and Windows 10 or 11 (x64)
